name: Hearts
description:
Hearts

    enumi1

  1. Hearth-Aunt — Holds guest-cup and house's temper; hospitality as power.

    She has never drawn a blade. She has never needed to. Her hospitality has ended more feuds than swords. She counts her guests in eights. The ninth chair is empty.

    Guest-right cost: She owes a blood-weight to the Mac Tern clan. If you help her pay it (a quest), she gives you a Guest-Token (Diamond). Guest-right cost: share a true story of a broken oath. If you refuse, start Grudge of the Hearth [4].

  2. Hill Guide — Thorn-staff and ten quiet shortcuts; the land as a map.

    He taps each stone before stepping. The stones talk to him. He learned the tongue from an Aeler outcast who went deaf and learned to listen with his feet. He never takes a ninth step in the same direction.

    Guest-right cost: A cup of tea and a moment of silence. If you speak during his listening, he refuses to guide—start Lost Ways [4].

  3. Feud-Broker — Knows the weight of a life in cattle and coin; peace as trade.

    His record is a row of notched sticks. Each notch is a death—or a birth. He has notched both sides of the same feud for forty years. He counts in eights. The ninth notch is a lie.

    Service: He will settle any dispute for a wergild of 3 cows (or 1 Supply). If you pay, gain +1 Position in the next negotiation. If you cheat him, the cairns remember—start Broker's Grudge [4].

  4. Reiver Band — Light on tack, heavy on nerve, laughing in the rain.

    They wear no colors. Their horses answer to whistles, not names. They raid Viterran supply trains and leave heather sprigs as signatures. They ride in eights. The ninth horse is a ghost.

    Alliance: They will raid a target of your choice—but demand a hostage (a PC becomes a temporary follower of the band). Refusal starts Reiver Hunt [4].

  5. Fire Warden — Braziers speak faster than riders; warning as weapon.

    She can light a signal with a single word. The word is a dead man's name. The dead man was a Viterran knight who burned her village. She lights eight beacons. The ninth would call the Hollow.

    Guest-right cost: She demands a name of someone who wronged your family. If you cannot give one, she refuses to share her fire—start Exposure [4] (cold).

  6. Wergild Keeper — Keeps tallies, ends grudges, starts others; law as math.

    His reckoning beads are sheep knuckles. He clicks them in his sleep. His grandmother taught him; she learned from an Aeler vent-prior. He counts in eights. The ninth bead is silence.

    Service: He can reckon a blood-weight for 1 Supply. On a success (Wits+Lore DV 3), he finds a hidden wergild that clears 2 segments of a Feud timer. On a Miss, he finds a weight you must settle—tick Wergild Breach [4].

  7. Dwarf Warden (Aeler Outcast) — Khaz-Vurim road; toll first, friendship later.

    Her hammer has a chip where she cracked a liar's skull. She never fixed it. She came to the surface for the sky—and stayed for the feuds. She breathes in eights. The ninth is the mountain's.

    Toll: 1 Supply or a story about a betrayal. She is collecting evidence for a case she will never bring. If you lie, she marks you—start Marked Notice [3].

  8. Oath-Singer — Verses bind hands and open gates; word as iron.

    Her tongue is forked—she can praise and curse in the same breath. Her songs are older than the Viterran crown. Each verse has eight lines. The ninth is the silence after.

    Guest-right cost: She asks you to sing a verse of your own people's oath-song. If you cannot, she refuses to witness any oath you make—start Unwitnessed [4].

  9. Lowland Factor — Buying iron blooms, selling trouble; coin as catalyst.

    He carries two books. One is for the clans. One is for the tax man. The third book is in his head; it lists every bribe he has ever taken. He counts in eights. The ninth entry is a death.

    Service: He can forge a Viterran tax waiver for 1 Boon. On a Miss, the forgery is discovered—start Royal Incursion [4].

    J
    Bride-Carrier — Peaceweaver walking bloodlines with a knife and a smile.

    Her knife has a wooden blade. The threat is real. She has walked between warring clans nine times. The ninth was a Viterran lord who wanted a wife. He got a treaty instead. She carries eight ribbons. The ninth is a scar.

    Guest-right cost: She demands a lock of hair from each PC (as a pledge of peace). Refusal starts a Bride-Price Feud [4].

    Q
    Lady of Tor — Clan-chief in cloak and mail; her nod is winter or spring.

    She lost a hand to a Viterran knight. Her iron hook has a built-in bell. The bell rings when she lies. It has never rung. She holds eight councilors. The ninth is the cairn.

    Guest-right cost: To speak with her, you must first offer a public apology for any wrong your people have done to her clan. If you refuse, she will not hear you—start Tor's Silence [4].

    K
    Council of Cairns — Graybeards and granite wills; they do not hurry.

    They have sentenced men to exile. The sentences take a year to deliver. The exile always knows before they speak. There are eight councilors. The ninth is the dead they serve.

    Cairn vote: The Council speaks for the dead. Any request for their judgment triggers a cairn vote (see table). They never accept bribes—only wergild.

    A
    Stone-Speaker — Aeler outcast envoy whose word moves roads and rates.

    He carries a tuning fork. Strike it, and the mountain answers. He has not seen his homeland in sixty years. He calls the mist his ceiling now. He counts his breaths in eights. The ninth is the mountain's answer.

    Guest-right cost: He asks for a memory of your homeland. If you give a true memory, he grants you a Stone-Clause (Diamond). If you lie, the mountain remembers—start Ancestral Grudge [4].
